data.narrative:
QuantWare is a Series B quantum computing company founded by Matt Rijlaarsdam and Alessandro Bruno that has raised $178M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 total comparable companies—3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using QuantWare's $178M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $338M. The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing space; while 6 same-sector peers exist, none meet minimum narrow-filter thresholds, and a broad sector median would lack specificity to QuantWare's stage and positioning.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $287M (low) to $389M (high), with a median of $338M. The single-method basis of this range represents the primary uncertainty—triangulation robustness would improve materially with access to a tighter peer set at Series B in quantum computing or with disclosed valuation data from portfolio-stage rounds. Key variables affecting valuation include technical milestones, IP position relative to the named peer set, and capital efficiency relative to sector norms.
